Create Cohort Labels for a Reporting Tree

Source: R/cohort_labels_tree.R
cohort_labels_tree.Rd

Create labels for a reporting tree, in which records are tabulated at different levels of detail: detailed cohorts, broader cohorts, and, optionally, cohort not stated.

Usage

cohort_labels_tree(
  breaks,
  nodes = NULL,
  open_left = FALSE,
  open_right = FALSE,
  format_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  format_multi = c("at_upper", "below_upper"),
  include_missing = TRUE
)

Arguments

breaks

Boundaries between cohorts. A numeric vector.

nodes

Labels for broad cohorts. A character vector, or NULL (the default), in which case there are no broad cohorts.

open_left

Whether first cohort is open on the left, i.e. has no lower limit. Default is FALSE.

open_right

Whether last cohort is open on the right, i.e. has no upper limit. Default is FALSE.

format_single

How to format label for single-year cohort. Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

format_multi

How to format the second number in a label for a multi-year cohort. With "at_upper" (the default), the second number is the upper limit of the cohort. With "below_upper", the second number is one year below the upper limit. See below for details.

include_missing

Whether to include a "Missing" category, representing cohort not stated. Default is TRUE.

Value

Character vector.

Details

The most detailed cohorts (the leaves of the tree) are created from breaks, open_left, and open_right, exactly as by cohort_labels(). Broader cohorts are supplied through nodes, as ordinary cohort labels. Broader cohorts can be given in any order, and can nest to any depth. Leaves do not need to be the same distance from the root.

Labels in nodes are interpreted using the same rules as are used to format the leaves, as set by format_single and format_multi. With the default format_multi = "at_upper", for instance, "2000-2010" means the cohort from the start of 2000 to the start of 2010. Labels in nodes are then converted into the same format as the leaves.

Each broad cohort must start and end at values in breaks (or be open, if open_left or open_right is TRUE), so that it is a union of detailed cohorts. It must contain at least two detailed cohorts, but not all of them, and broad cohorts must nest: any two either do not overlap, or one contains the other.

The root of the tree, representing records with no information on cohort, is labelled "Missing". Unlike cohort_labels(), cohort_labels_tree() includes "Missing" by default, since most reporting trees in practice have a category for cohort not stated.

Labels are returned in the same order as cohort_set_order_tree(): detailed cohorts, then broad cohorts (each after the cohorts inside it), then "Missing".

Rules for formatting output

Single-year cohorts

format_singleRuleExample
"lower"[a,a+1) -> "a"[2020,2021) -> "2020"
"upper"[a,a+1) -> "<a+1>"[2020,2021) -> "2021"

Multi-year cohorts

format_multiRuleExample
"at_upper"[a,b) -> "a-b"[2020,2025) -> "2020-2025"
"below_upper"[a,b) -> "a-<b-1>"[2020,2025) -> "2020-2024"

Open cohorts

Interval typeRuleExample
open on left(-Inf,a) -> "<a"(-Inf,2020) -> "<2020"
open on right[a,Inf) -> "a+"[2020,Inf) -> "2020+"

See also

  • cohort_labels() Create labels without broad cohorts

  • cohort_set_order_tree() Order existing labels as a tree

  • cohort_diagnose_values() Check labels, including with valid_tree = TRUE

  • age_labels_tree() Age equivalent of cohort_labels_tree()

  • period_labels_tree() Period equivalent of cohort_labels_tree()

Examples

## year of birth: 10-year cohorts, a broad group
## for births before 1960, and not stated
cohort_labels_tree(
  breaks = seq(1940, 2000, 10),
  nodes = "<1960",
  open_left = TRUE
)
#> [1] "<1940"     "1940-1950" "1950-1960" "1960-1970" "1970-1980" "1980-1990"
#> [7] "1990-2000" "<1960"     "Missing"
